extracted.intended_audience: judges, court staff, legal professionals, and policymakers (general public interested in courtroom fairness)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for judges and courtroom actors on applying procedural-justice principles so people in court are treated with dignity and come away believing justice was served. Based on a TED Talk describing four practical steps used in a Newark courtroom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat everyone with dignity and respect
rubrics_metrics.description: How can we ensure everyone is treated with dignity and respect? (applies in halls of justice around the world)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page frames this as a primary goal of courtroom practice: ensuring people who come to court are treated with dignity and respect. No further operationalization is provided on the page itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural justice — four simple, thoughtful steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles of "procedural justice" — four simple, thoughtful steps that redefined the everyday business of her courtroom in Newark, changing lives along the way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The talk is presented as centered on four concrete steps (not enumerated on this page) which implement procedural-justice principles in day-to-day courtroom practice; the page emphasizes these as practical, actionable changes that produced measurable effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court behavior influences public response
rubrics_metrics.description: "When the court behaves differently, naturally people respond differently,"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit evaluative standard: judges and court staff should change their behavior if the goal is to alter public conduct and perceptions. The page uses this claim to justify adopting different courtroom practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate that justice will be served
rubrics_metrics.description: "We want people to enter our halls of justice ... and know that justice will be served there."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A criterion for courtroom interactions is that participants leave with confidence that the system is fair and will deliver justice; the page presents this as an outcome of applying procedural-justice steps and respectful behavior.
